headline: April was dominated by Anthropic's withheld Claude Mythos model and a dense release cycle of GPT-5.5, Opus 4.7, the new Codex and Claude Design. Underneath it, the shows converged on the harness around the model, and the usage-based pricing and compute limits that agentic workloads now force, as the real story.

themes.title: Claude Mythos and Project Glasswing
themes.body: Anthropic announced Claude Mythos Preview as a step-change model withheld from general release and offered to about 40 partners via Project Glasswing for cyber defense. NLW reviewed its zero-day findings and argued that fear serves no one, while Practical AI weighed the hype against the substance. Jensen Huang and Dwarkesh Patel framed their China export debate around Mythos, Cameron Berg examined its system card welfare findings, and AIDB later reported unauthorized Discord access via a third-party vendor and a White House-Anthropic detente.

themes.title: Harness engineering becomes the discipline
themes.body: NLW positioned harness engineering, designing the systems, tools and context around a model, as the successor to prompt and context engineering, citing HumanLayer, LangChain, OpenAI and Anthropic's Managed Agents. OpenAI's Ryan Lopopolo described a million-line app built with zero human-written code in Codex. Notion's Simon Last and Sarah Sachs recounted four to five harness rebuilds since 2022. Practical AI dissected the leaked Claude Code harness, and NLW used Cursor's SDK to propose 'Harness as a Service' as a new infrastructure category. DHH told Gergely Orosz he now works agent-first.

themes.title: GPT-5.5, Opus 4.7 and the release wave
themes.body: The month brought Claude Opus 4.7, OpenAI's new Codex app with Mac computer use, Anthropic's Claude Design, ChatGPT Images 2.0 and GPT-5.5. NLW tested GPT-5.5 in Codex and noted Anthropic's post-mortem confirming Claude Code quality issues. He called Images 2.0 the first image model for the agentic era and argued coding tools are converging. Andon Labs reported Vending-Bench results for GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.7 on Cognitive Revolution. Earlier, Meta's Muse Spark and Z.ai's open-source GLM 5.1 arrived.

themes.title: The end of flat-fee AI
themes.body: NLW argued the AI subsidy era is ending because agentic usage consumes more tokens than flat-fee plans cover, citing GitHub Copilot's move to usage-based billing and Anthropic's compute strains. Anthropic also shifted enterprise customers to usage-based pricing. SAP CTO Philipp Herzig described moving from seat-based to hybrid consumption pricing, and Notion uses usage-based credits for its agents. NLW's headless agents episode questioned per-seat SaaS pricing, while ServiceNow's Bill McDermott argued enterprise platforms are not threatened by the 'SaaS apocalypse'.

themes.title: Compute, power and capital
themes.body: AIDB tracked Anthropic reaching $30B ARR with a multi-gigawatt Google/Broadcom TPU deal, Google's investment of up to $40 billion in Anthropic, OpenAI's $122B round and 30-gigawatt compute target, and Nvidia hitting $5 trillion. The White House invoked the Defense Production Act for grid infrastructure as DeepSeek V4 arrived near-frontier at a fraction of the price. Jensen Huang defended Nvidia's supply chain moat against TPUs, MatX's Reiner Pope worked through inference economics, and Practical AI covered Allbirds' pivot to a neocloud. On The Moonshot Podcast, Tammo Spalink and Raj Apte recounted X's Positron inference chips and Bodger's automated chip design, and Fort Felker and Raj Apte the Makani energy kite and Malta molten-salt storage.

themes.title: Enterprise adoption and the leadership gap
themes.body: NLW introduced Superintelligent's maturity maps, drawn from 480+ studies, showing gaps in people investment, data and outcome measurement, and argued enterprise AI has a leadership problem. A PwC study found the top fifth of companies capture about 75% of AI's economic gains. Ramp's Glass platform was offered as a model for raising the floor across an organization. Shopify CTO Mikhail Parakhin described an unlimited token budget, and Block's world-model org chart was contrasted with Every's parallel org chart of personal agents.

themes.title: Personal agent systems: skills, context, memory
themes.body: Nufar Gaspar ran an agent skills masterclass and introduced AIDB's Agent OS, seven layers from identity to automations, arguing the system matters more than the tool. NLW proposed a personal context portfolio of ten markdown files served via an MCP server to avoid context lock-in. His Agent Madness review named memory as the main infrastructure gap. Steve Newman demoed a Claude Code-built attention firewall, and Granola's Sam Stephenson discussed agent context and memory in note-taking.

themes.title: Backlash, politics and safety
themes.body: NLW covered the attacks on Sam Altman's home and argued AI has become a cauldron for broader economic grievance, a topic Nathan Labenz's AI in the AM also discussed with Stanford's Andy Hall on AI governance. NLW critiqued OpenAI's industrial policy document against dire American sentiment, and read Alex Imas on a growing relational sector of human work. Ajeya Cotra described a 'crunch time' when AI automates AI R&D, and Nathan Labenz discussed his p(doom) and the Pentagon-Anthropic standoff.

themes.title: Physical AI, world models and science
themes.body: Applied Intuition's Qasar Younis and Peter Ludwig described autonomy models for cars, trucks, mining and defense, and Comma AI's Harald Schäfer explained training driving policies inside a learned world-model simulator. NVIDIA's Sanja Fidler told Turing Post that transformers and world models are not competing, and traced driving simulation toward the interactive Alpa Dreams model. Moonlake's Chris Manning argued for multimodal, interactive world models. Liam Fedus said AI science needs closed-loop physical experiments, and Noetik described a $50M model licensing deal with GSK. The Moonshot Podcast covered X's science moonshots: an AI 'virtual cell' for biomanufacturing and ML-programmed crops, AI software that prices building designs in seconds, and water-from-air and seawater-fuel projects ended by kill criteria.

implications: Budget AI as metered consumption, not seats. Vendors including GitHub, Anthropic, SAP and Notion are moving to usage-based or hybrid pricing, so agentic workloads need token forecasting, cost attribution and guardrails before they scale across teams.

Treat the harness as owned architecture. Tools, context, memory, evals and review agents determined outcomes in the OpenAI and Notion accounts, and harnesses are being rebuilt repeatedly, so keep them modular and model-agnostic rather than tied to one vendor's app.

Plan for capability that arrives gated. Mythos shows frontier models may reach selected partners first under security programmes, so security teams should track vendor disclosure practices and prepare for faster discovery of vulnerabilities in their own software.

Invest in people and shared platforms, not only licences. The adoption studies point to gaps in leadership, training, data and outcome measurement, and organization-level platforms like Ramp's Glass raise the floor more than individual tool access does.

Standardize skills, context and memory as reusable assets. Skill libraries, portable context files and MCP servers reduce lock-in across converging agent tools, but they need governance, testing and ownership like any other shared enterprise component.

episodes.title: How Harness-as-a-Service Will Change Agents
episodes.summary: Headlines cover big tech Q1 earnings from Google, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta, showing strong AI-driven cloud growth and rising capex. The main segment uses Cursor's new SDK to propose 'Harness as a Service' as a new infrastructure category, comparing the OpenClaw era to hobbyist computing.

episodes.title: AI Lab Power Rankings
episodes.summary: Headlines cover the amended Microsoft–OpenAI agreement, OpenAI models arriving on AWS Bedrock, Amazon Quick, and pushback on a WSJ report on OpenAI's missed targets. The main segment presents NLW's first AI Lab Power Rankings across nine weighted categories, comparing AI-generated scores with his own.

episodes.title: Reiner Pope – The math behind how LLMs are trained and served
episodes.summary: In a blackboard lecture, MatX CEO Reiner Pope walks Dwarkesh Patel through roofline analysis of LLM inference: batch size, KV cache, MoE layout on GPU racks, scale-up vs. scale-out, and pipeline parallelism. They estimate frontier models are ~100x over-trained beyond Chinchilla, deduce memory costs from API pricing, and discuss parallels between neural nets and cryptography.

episodes.title: Silicon Horizons
episodes.summary: Astro Teller talks with Tammo Spalink about Project Positron, an X effort begun around 2015 to build inference chips optimized for response time as 'brains for robots', which pivoted to cloud inference and graduated to Google Brain. He then talks with Raj Apte about Project Bodger, which uses inverse design and computer search to automate chip design as Moore's law ends and AI drives demand for compute.

episodes.title: Building Pi, and what makes self-modifying software so fascinating
episodes.summary: Gergely Orosz talks with Mario Zechner, creator of the minimalist self-modifying coding agent Pi that powers OpenClaw, and Armin Ronacher, creator of Flask and a Pi user. They discuss why Pi was built after Claude Code became unpredictable, what Armin learned from 30+ engineering teams adopting agents (falling quality, review fatigue, automation bias), friction and complexity, agent-generated open source contributions, the case for slowing down, and MCP versus CLIs.

episodes.title: The AI Subsidy Era is Over
episodes.summary: NLW argues AI's subsidy era is ending as agentic usage drives token consumption beyond what flat-fee plans cover. He covers GitHub Copilot's shift to usage-based billing, Anthropic's compute strains, market reactions, implications for AI job displacement, and five practical steps for enterprises.

episodes.title: David Sinclair: The GLP-1 Side Effect No One Talks About, What AI Found in His Lab, and Reversing Blindness | Q&A EP #251
episodes.summary: An audience Q&A with Harvard geneticist David Sinclair and Peter Diamandis, recorded at the 2026 Abundance360 Summit. Sinclair covers GLP-1 drugs and a rare blindness side effect, AI-driven drug discovery and biological-age measurement in his lab, telomeres, genetics versus lifestyle, OSK/ER-100 reprogramming results in ALS and macular degeneration models, hormone replacement, mindset, and indoor environments and hormetic stress.

episodes.title: How DeepSeek V4 Connects to the US Power Grid
episodes.summary: Headlines cover Google's up-to-$40 billion investment in Anthropic, Amazon's compute-for-equity deal, Meta renting Graviton CPUs, the AI trade's return and Nvidia hitting $5 trillion. The main episode links the White House invoking the Defense Production Act for grid infrastructure with the release of DeepSeek V4, near-frontier at a fraction of the price, and Beijing's moves to curb US investment and block Meta's Manus acquisition.

episodes.title: Physical AI that Moves the World — Qasar Younis & Peter Ludwig, Applied Intuition
episodes.summary: Applied Intuition co-founders Qasar Younis (CEO) and Peter Ludwig (CTO) describe their physical AI company: simulation tooling, a vehicle operating system, and autonomy models for cars, trucks, mining, agriculture and defense. They discuss LiDAR, statistical validation, world models, onboard model efficiency, coding agent adoption and founder advice.

episodes.title: David Sinclair on the Longevity Pill, Age Reversal Timelines, and Updated Protocols | EP #250
episodes.summary: Peter Diamandis interviews Harvard geneticist David Sinclair on stage at the 2026 Abundance360 Summit. Sinclair discusses the imminent first human epigenetic reprogramming trial (Life Biosciences' ER-100 for blindness), a cheaper small-molecule reprogramming cocktail entered in the Healthspan XPRIZE, whether lifespan has an upper limit, and the privately funded Friends of Sinclair Lab model after his federal funding was cut. He closes with his personal longevity protocol: resveratrol, NMN, metformin/berberine, nattokinase, mostly vegan diet, no alcohol, stress reduction and social connection.

episodes.title: Where the Economy Thrives After AI
episodes.summary: NLW critiques the AI jobs discourse for focusing on destruction over creation and argues AI shifts economic constraints from supply to demand. He then reads economist Alex Imas's essay 'What Will Be Scarce?', which uses structural change economics and mimetic desire to argue AI will grow a 'relational sector' of human-intensive work as commodity production gets cheap.

episodes.title: AI in the AM: 99% off search, GPT-5.5 is \"clean\", model welfare analysis, & efficient analog compute
episodes.summary: A live 'AI in the AM' episode recorded the day after GPT-5.5's release. Anna Patterson explains Ceramic.ai's cheap, fast search for LLMs; Lukas Petersson reports Andon Labs' Vending-Bench results for GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.7 and AI-run stores; Zvi Mowshowitz discusses model welfare; Naveen Verma explains EnCharge AI's analog in-memory computing.

episodes.title: How to Build a Personal Agentic Operating System
episodes.summary: In an Operators bonus episode, Nufar Gaspar introduces AIDB's free Agent OS program, a tool-neutral framework for building a personal agentic operating system. She walks through seven layers (identity, context, skills, memory, connections, verification, automations) using a chief-of-staff agent as the running example, arguing that converging agentic tools make the underlying system more important than the tool.

episodes.title: How Headless Agents Will Change Work
episodes.summary: Headlines cover OpenAI's 30-gigawatt compute target, power and turbine bottlenecks at GE Vernova, Google's split training/inference TPUs, Google's 75% AI-generated code stat, OpenAI's Privacy Filter open-weights model, and a possible Mistral-xAI tie-up. The main episode explores headless software and agents through Salesforce Headless 360, OpenAI workspace agents, Microsoft hosted agents and Google's Gemini Enterprise platform, and debates implications for per-seat SaaS pricing and who captures value.

episodes.title: What I Learned Testing GPT-5.5
episodes.summary: NLW reviews OpenAI's GPT-5.5 ('Spud'): benchmarks versus Opus 4.7 and Mythos, pricing and token efficiency, first reactions on coding, long-running tasks, design and planning, and OpenAI's humbler, democratization-focused communications. He shares his own tests in Codex across writing, strategy, web apps, research art books and data analysis, and notes Anthropic's post-mortem confirming Claude Code quality issues.

episodes.title: Does Learning Require Feeling? Cameron Berg on the latest AI Consciousness & Welfare Research
episodes.summary: Nathan Labenz and Cameron Berg survey recent AI consciousness and welfare research, including Anthropic's introspection and functional emotions work, steering resistance, and model welfare findings in the Claude Mythos and Opus 4.7 system cards. Berg previews unpublished work on valence signatures in reinforcement learning that map onto mouse neuroscience, argues that learning and feeling may be identical, and discusses his documentary Am I?.

episodes.title: AIE Europe Debrief + Agent Labs Thesis: Unsupervised Learning x Latent Space Crossover Special (2026)
episodes.summary: In an Unsupervised Learning crossover, host Jacob Effron interviews swyx after AI Engineer Europe about the state of the AI coding wars, the agent lab playbook of training own models, selling to agents, SaaS versus vibe-coded replacements, Anthropic's restricted Mythos release, open models' rising share, dark factories, multi-turn RL, and world models.

episodes.title: Iran's AI Supply Chain Threat, Claude vs. SaaS, and Elon's $60B Cursor Bet | EP #249
episodes.summary: Moonshot Mates roundtable covering Anthropic's Claude Design and frontier labs encroaching on SaaS, AI's effect on entry-level jobs, Grok's roadmap, OpenAI departures and ChatGPT Images 2.0, and SpaceX's $60B option on Cursor. It also covers AI data center capex, the Iran war's supply shocks (oil, helium, gas), UAP disclosure, China's solar and robotics push, Apple's CEO change, and listener critiques about entrepreneurship and ivory-tower optimism.

episodes.title: SAP: Bringing the ‘Operating System’ of a Company into the AI Era with CTO Philipp Herzig
episodes.summary: Sarah Guo interviews SAP CTO Philipp Herzig on why SAP has endured through technology shifts, how AI changes enterprise software at the UI, business-process and data layers, and the challenges of scaling AI in large enterprises. They discuss evals and 'agent mining', tool calling vs computer use, SAP's relational pre-trained transformer for tabular predictions, and SAP's move from seat-based to hybrid consumption pricing. The transcript ends around 39:45, before the final segments.

episodes.title: The mythos of Mythos and Allbirds takes flight to the neocloud
episodes.summary: Daniel and Chris discuss Allbirds' pivot from footwear to AI compute infrastructure and the rise of neoclouds, then Anthropic's withheld Mythos model and Project Glasswing. They also cover 'tokenmaxxing' in engineering teams and a federal ruling that AI chat logs are not protected by attorney-client privilege.

episodes.title: What GPT Images 2 Unlocks
episodes.summary: Headlines cover SpaceX's deal with Cursor including an option to acquire it at $60 billion, SpaceX IPO disclosures, unauthorized Discord access to Claude Mythos via a third-party vendor, Sam Altman's 'fear-based marketing' critique of Anthropic, and Google's Deep Research Max. The main episode reviews OpenAI's ChatGPT Images 2.0, its record Arena lead, realism, text and world knowledge, and argues it is the first image model for the agentic era via pipelines like Image 2 plus Codex for UI.

episodes.title: Shopify’s AI Phase Transition: 2026 Usage Explosion, Unlimited Opus-4.6 Token Budget, Tangle, Tangent, SimGym — with Mikhail Parakhin, Shopify CTO
episodes.summary: Shopify CTO Mikhail Parakhin walks through Shopify's internal AI adoption data, including a December 2025 inflection in tool usage and an unlimited token budget with an Opus 4.6 minimum, and argues for expensive-model PR review over parallel agent swarms. He describes the Tangle experimentation platform, the Tangent auto-research loop, the SimGym customer simulator, Shopify's use of Liquid AI models, and Bing Sydney history.

episodes.title: Ocean Fuel, Desert Rain
episodes.summary: Astro Teller talks with Neil Treat and Claudia Truesdell about H2E, X's attempt to harvest drinking water from air using sunlight for a penny a liter, and then with Kathy Hannun about Foghorn, which turned seawater into carbon-neutral methanol but could not reach a competitive cost. Both projects were wound down via kill criteria and their results published openly.

episodes.title: Designing Data-intensive Applications with Martin Kleppmann
episodes.summary: Gergely Orosz interviews Martin Kleppmann about his startups (GoTestIt, Rapportive), working on stream processing at LinkedIn alongside Kafka, and writing Designing Data-Intensive Applications and its second edition co-written with Chris Riccomini. They discuss cloud-native architecture, scaling up and down, the trouble with distributed systems, ethics, formal verification in the AI era, local-first software, and computer science education.

episodes.title: AI Could Change Education Forever – Neeru Khosla Explains Why
episodes.summary: Ksenia Se interviews Neeru Khosla, co-founder of the CK-12 Foundation, about how AI can reveal how students think, CK-12's AI tutor Flexi, and why standardized testing and public-school inertia slow change. They discuss prompting as a learning skill, AI literacy, the five C's, philanthropy and free education, and Khosla's path from molecular biology to education.

episodes.title: How Apple's AI Strategy Changes with a New CEO
episodes.summary: Headlines cover OpenAI's Chronicle screen-memory feature in Codex, Anthropic's Cowork Live Artifacts, a White House-Anthropic detente over Mythos, the Vercel breach, DeepSeek and Cursor fundraising, and chip/memory shortages. The main segment discusses Tim Cook stepping down for John Ternus and Apple's AI position, followed by Google's AI coding strike team, Amazon's $25 billion Anthropic deal, and Meta's layoffs and trades training program.

episodes.title: What To Build First With Claude Design
episodes.summary: NLW reviews Anthropic's newly launched Claude Design, its features (Socratic onboarding questions, multiple variations, per-design tweak sliders, design-system ingestion, Claude Code handoff), early user creations and complaints (rate limits, exports, no native image generation). He compares it to Canva, Figma, Google Stitch, Genspark and Manus, and suggests seven things to try first.

episodes.title: 🔬 Training Transformers to solve 95% failure rate of Cancer Trials — Ron Alfa & Daniel Bear, Noetik
episodes.summary: On a Latent Space Science episode, Noetik co-founder and CEO Ron Alfa and VP of AI Daniel Bear argue cancer drugs mostly fail because of poor patient selection, and describe generating multimodal spatial tumor data in-house to train self-supervised patient-level models. They cover the OctoVC virtual cell model, the autoregressive Tario model, the PerturbMap mouse platform, and a $50M model licensing deal with GSK.

episodes.title: How the Best Companies Use AI
episodes.summary: NLW examines what separates AI-leading companies, drawing on PwC's study, McKinsey's AI Transformation Manifesto, and George Sivulka's a16z piece on institutional versus individual AI. The centerpiece is Ramp's internal Glass platform, an organization-level harness with SSO integrations, a skills marketplace, memory and automations, built on the principle of raising the floor rather than lowering the ceiling.

episodes.title: Vibe-Coding an Attention Firewall, w/ Steve Newman, creator of The Curve
episodes.summary: Steve Newman, creator of Writely and founder of the Golden Gate Institute for AI, demos his personal Claude Code-built toolkit: an attention firewall, a newsletter summarizing reader, an agent status dashboard, data mirroring and universal logging. He and Nathan Labenz discuss security trade-offs, anti-tokenmaxxing, software jobs, AGI skepticism, robotics and AI's climate impact.

episodes.title: Agent Building Trends [Operator Bonus Episode]
episodes.summary: NLW reviews patterns from about 100 submissions to his Agent Madness bracket, judged by AI models. Themes include builders creating digital employees and org charts, 'markets of one' personal tools, memory as the main infrastructure gap, multi-agent debate as architecture, non-technical domain-expert builders, and physical-world crossover; he previews the Elite Eight projects.

episodes.title: Sam Altman’s Attack, Amazon vs. Starlink, and What Opus 4.7 Actually Means | #248
episodes.summary: Moonshot Mates roundtable opening with Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.7 release, then the Stanford 2026 AI Index, young workers squeezed out of jobs, the Molotov attack on Sam Altman's house and AI backlash, and local and state data center bans. Other segments cover workers training their AI replacements, an AI-run store, Jack Dorsey's flattened org, Amazon's Globalstar deal with Apple versus Starlink, Google's TurboQuant, AI religion apps, an AI-assisted cancer cure, Allbirds' AI pivot, the Enhanced Games, and a closing debate on human speciation (longevity, BCI, space, uploading).

episodes.title: How to Use Opus 4.7 and the New Codex
episodes.summary: NLW reviews two releases: OpenAI's new Codex app (Mac computer use, in-app browser, image generation, heartbeats/thread automations, projectless chats) and Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.7. He highlights the 'monothread' and Codex chief-of-staff patterns, Opus 4.7's benchmark gains, tips for using it, and the contrasting UI philosophies of Codex versus the Claude desktop app.

episodes.title: Scaling Global Organizations in the Age of AI with ServiceNow Chairman and CEO Bill McDermott
episodes.summary: Sarah Guo interviews ServiceNow CEO Bill McDermott about his early career (buying a deli at 16, getting hired at Xerox) and leadership in the AI era. McDermott argues enterprise platforms are not threatened by the 'SaaS apocalypse', positions ServiceNow as an 'AI control tower' for agentic business, and discusses agents reshaping headcount and enterprise AI adoption.

episodes.title: AI's Great Divergence
episodes.summary: Headlines cover Allbirds' pivot to an AI neocloud, OpenAI's Agents SDK sandbox update, pay-per-click ChatGPT ads, the chilling effect of China's Manus investigation, and Jensen Huang's call for US-China dialogue on the Dwarkesh podcast. The main episode examines divergence in AI via the Stanford AI Index (expert vs public optimism, jagged frontier, entry-level jobs) and a PwC study finding the top fifth of companies capture about 75% of AI's economic gains.

episodes.title: Open Source Self-Driving with Comma AI
episodes.summary: Daniel and Chris interview Harald Schäfer, CTO of Comma AI, about OpenPilot, the open-source driver-assistance stack running on Comma's aftermarket device. They cover end-to-end driving models, training policies inside a learned world-model simulator, edge compute limits, and open problems in controls, reinforcement learning and continual learning.

episodes.title: AI Populism Turns Violent
episodes.summary: NLW covers the Molotov cocktail and shooting attacks on Sam Altman's home, Altman's blog response, and the online debate blaming AI doomers, journalists and the AI industry. He argues AI has become a cauldron for broader economic grievance and perceived inequality, and outlines research-based responses: democratic channels for AI governance, addressing economic trajectory, and breaking the moral frame.

episodes.title: Vibe Coding Gets an Upgrade
episodes.summary: Headlines cover rumors of Claude Opus 4.7 and an Anthropic design tool, OpenAI's GPT-5 for cyber, Anthropic's usage-based enterprise pricing amid a GPU compute crunch, and Maine's statewide data center moratorium. The main episode covers the redesigned Claude Code desktop app for parallel agent work, Claude Code routines, Lovable's desktop app and payments, Google and Microsoft updates, and enterprise hardening of vibe coding, arguing coding tools are converging.

episodes.title: Welcome to AI in the AM: RL for EE, Oversight w/out Nationalization, & the first AI-Run Retail Store
episodes.summary: Nathan Labenz and Prakash Narayanan's live stream features Sergiy Nesterenko of Quilter on reinforcement learning for PCB design, Andy Hall of Stanford on AI governance, political persuasion and agent governance, and Lukas Peterson and Axel Backlund of Andon Labs on their AI-run San Francisco store. The hosts also discuss attacks on Sam Altman's home, Mythos, and AI in trading.

episodes.title: Jensen Huang – TPU competition, why we should sell chips to China, & Nvidia’s supply chain moat
episodes.summary: Jensen Huang discusses Nvidia's supply chain commitments, competition from TPUs and custom ASICs, the CUDA ecosystem, why Nvidia invests in labs and neoclouds rather than becoming a hyperscaler, and GPU allocation. A long debate with Dwarkesh Patel covers whether selling AI chips to China harms US security, framed around Anthropic's Claude Mythos.

episodes.title: Notion’s Token Town: 5 Rebuilds, 100+ Tools, MCP vs CLIs and the Software Factory Future — Simon Last & Sarah Sachs of Notion
episodes.summary: Simon Last and Sarah Sachs of Notion discuss the launch of Notion custom agents, the four-to-five rebuilds of Notion's agent harness since 2022, their eval and model behavior engineering practice, MCP versus CLIs, usage-based credit pricing, retrieval for agents, and meeting notes as data capture.

episodes.title: Breaking New Ground
episodes.summary: Astro Teller talks with architect Michelle Kaufmann about her path from Frank Gehry's office and a failed prefab home company to X's Genie project, which spun out as Flux and built 'intelligent clay' software that priced and engineered building designs in seconds. He then talks with Adrian Walker and Julia Ling of Anori, an X venture using AI and data sharing to front-load building constraints, automate permit checks and address the housing crisis.

episodes.title: Elon Musk vs. Sam Altman, AI Job Loss, and OpenAI’s $852B Valuation | EP #247
episodes.summary: A Moonshot Mates roundtable (Peter Diamandis, Salim Ismail, Dave Blundin, Alexander Wissner-Gross) covering xAI's rebuild and Colossus 2 models, the Musk v. OpenAI lawsuit, Anthropic and OpenAI valuations, record AI venture investment, and the AI-and-jobs debate including Marc Andreessen's view and Sam Altman's call for a new social contract. Later segments cover energy (solar, micro reactors, iron-air batteries), AI drug discovery and the OpenAI Foundation, Chinese humanoid robots, quantum risk to Bitcoin, and an 'abundance corner' on vertical farming, AI tutors and EV growth.

episodes.title: Harness Engineering 101
episodes.summary: A primer on harness engineering, the practice of designing the systems, tools and context around a model, positioned as the successor to prompt and context engineering. NLW covers the big-model vs big-harness debate, frameworks from HumanLayer, LangChain and OpenAI, evidence like Blitzy's SWE-bench Pro score, and Anthropic's Managed Agents as a meta-harness.

episodes.title: The New AI Org Chart
episodes.summary: A long-reads episode on how AI changes the org chart. NLW reads Jack Dorsey and Roelof Botha's essay on Block replacing hierarchy's information-routing role with a company world model and three roles, then contrasts it with Every's bottom-up experience of a parallel org chart of personal agents.

episodes.title: It's Crunch Time: Ajeya Cotra on RSI & AI-Powered AI Safety Work, from the 80,000 Hours Podcast
episodes.summary: A cross-post of Rob Wiblin's 80,000 Hours interview with Ajeya Cotra on AI timelines, why forecasters disagree so widely about AI-driven growth, and a 'crunch time' when AI automates AI R&D. They discuss transparency requirements, redirecting AI labour toward safety and defense, Open Philanthropy's role, and Cotra's career, sabbatical and views on effective altruism.

episodes.title: SpaceX Goes Public, Claude’s Mythos Release, and the US Data Center Delay | EP #246
episodes.summary: A Moonshot Mates roundtable (Peter Diamandis, Salim Ismail, Dave Blundin, Alexander Wissner-Gross) on SpaceX's planned $2 trillion IPO and the coming IPO wars, the Artemis II crewed lunar flyby and NASA's plans, and the April 2026 model wars led by Anthropic's withheld Claude Mythos and Project Glasswing. It also covers Anthropic overtaking OpenAI in ARR, Sora's shutdown, Sam Altman's cyber/bio warnings, the one-person unicorn Medvi, Terafab with Intel, US data center delays, Google's AI chip lead, abundance stories and viewer AMA questions.

episodes.title: Why Enterprise AI Has a Leadership Problem
episodes.summary: Headlines: the SaaSpocalypse narrative fades, Anthropic's tender offer undersubscribed, Anthropic hires Eric Boyd and a Workday executive, Musk amends his OpenAI suit, and Intel joins Musk's Terafab. The main segment compares enterprise AI studies from a16z, KPMG, Writer, and WalkMe, arguing enterprise AI faces a leadership problem and underinvestment in people.

episodes.title: All of AI's New Models and Tools
episodes.summary: Headlines cover a retracted Axios report on OpenAI withholding Spud, Perplexity Computer doubling revenue, GitHub straining under agentic coding, and Anthropic losing an appeals round against the Pentagon. The main segment reviews Meta's Muse Spark, Z.ai's open-source GLM 5.1, Anthropic's Claude Managed Agents, and Google's Notebooks in Gemini.

episodes.title: #495 – Vikings, Ragnar, Berserkers, Valhalla & the Warriors of the Viking Age
episodes.summary: Historian and podcaster Lars Brownworth talks with Lex Fridman about the Viking Age from the Lindisfarne raid in 793 to its end, covering longship technology, Ragnar Lothbrok, the Great Heathen Army, Rollo and Normandy, Norse religion and Valhalla, and voyages to Greenland and North America. They also discuss the Varangian Guard and the Byzantine Empire, Brownworth's early history podcast, and the great man theory of history and human nature.

episodes.title: The Agentic Economy: How AI Agents Will Transform the Financial System with Circle Co-Founder and CEO Jeremy Allaire
episodes.summary: Elad Gil interviews Circle co-founder and CEO Jeremy Allaire about stablecoins as full-reserve internet-native dollars, USDC's reserves and use cases, and blockchains as operating systems. Allaire argues an emerging agentic economy needs new financial infrastructure and presents Circle's Arc blockchain, then covers tokenization of real-world assets, inference as proof of work, a renegotiated social contract and double-digit GDP growth potential.

episodes.title: Post-Mortem of Anthropic's Claude Code Leak
episodes.summary: Daniel and Chris break down the April 2026 leak of Claude Code's source via a source map file, coinciding with a malicious Axios npm release. They discuss what the leaked agent harness reveals about memory management and agent design, the open-source clean-room rewrites, and Anthropic's dispute with the US Department of Defense over a supply chain risk designation.

episodes.title: OpenAI's New Deal
episodes.summary: Headlines cover Anthropic hitting $30B ARR and a multi-gigawatt Google/Broadcom TPU deal, WSJ analysis of OpenAI and Anthropic financials, Gemma 4 productization, Meta's Avocado model and token-maxing culture. The main segment critiques OpenAI's 'Industrial Policy for the Intelligence Age' document against dire American sentiment on AI, reviewing its proposals.

episodes.title: Should We Be Scared of Anthropic's Mythos?
episodes.summary: Anthropic formally announced Claude Mythos Preview, a step-change model withheld from general release and offered to ~40 partners via Project Glasswing for cyber defense. NLW reviews its benchmarks, system card safety findings, zero-day discoveries, and reactions ranging from fear to marketing skepticism, government-power debates, and his conclusion that fear serves no one.

episodes.title: Calm AI for Crazy Days: Inside Granola's Design Philosophy, with co-founder Sam Stephenson
episodes.summary: Nathan Labenz interviews Granola co-founder and designer Sam Stephenson about the AI note-taking app's minimalist design philosophy, growth through note sharing, and recipes. They discuss transcription providers and costs, privacy and consent, agent context and memory, AI's effect on product design work, and the risk of big tech dominating AI.

episodes.title: Chasing the Wind, Storing the Sun
episodes.summary: Astro Teller talks with Fort Felker about Makani, X's tethered energy-kite moonshot for harvesting wind, its testing journey and why it was shut down in 2020. He then talks with Raj Apte about Project Malta, a molten-salt thermal energy storage system based on Bob Laughlin's reversible heat engine idea, later spun out as a company.

episodes.title: DHH’s new way of writing code
episodes.summary: Gergely Orosz talks with David Heinemeier Hansson (DHH) about Omarchy, Ruby on Rails, 37signals' history with Basecamp and HEY, and the company's designer-as-builder model. DHH explains why he went agent-first after Opus 4.5 and agent harnesses arrived, describes his tmux/OpenCode/Claude Code workflow and CLIs for 37signals products, and discusses senior vs. junior developers, 'peak programmer', hiring, and avoiding burnout.

episodes.title: Michael Nielsen – How science actually progresses
episodes.summary: Michael Nielsen and Dwarkesh Patel discuss how science recognizes progress despite long, ambiguous verification loops, using Michelson-Morley, Darwin, Prout and Ptolemy vs. Copernicus. They consider implications for AI-driven science (AlphaFold), the vastness of the tech tree and alien tech stacks, quantum computing's origins, open science and credit, and how to learn deeply.

episodes.title: Extreme Harness Engineering for Token Billionaires: 1M LOC, 1B toks/day, 0% human code, 0% human review — Ryan Lopopolo, OpenAI Frontier & Symphony
episodes.summary: OpenAI's Ryan Lopopolo describes building a million-line Electron app over five months with zero human-written code using Codex, and the harness engineering practices that made it work: fast builds, observability, skills, review agents and encoding non-functional requirements as text. He introduces Symphony, an Elixir-based agent orchestrator distributed as a spec, and OpenAI Frontier, the enterprise agent platform.

episodes.title: How AI Is Bringing Extinct Animals Back (And What Comes Next) | Ben Lamm (Colossal) | EP #245
episodes.summary: Recorded live at the 2026 Abundance360 Summit, Peter Diamandis interviews Colossal Biosciences CEO Ben Lamm about de-extinction (dire wolves, woolly mammoth, Tasmanian tiger, dodo, moa) and Colossal's AI-powered synthetic biology platform. Topics include spin-out Breaking for plastic degradation, the UAE bio vault deal, artificial wombs, the ViaGen cloning acquisition, gene drives against invasive species, disease resistance for amphibians, and embryo health technology for IVF.

episodes.title: Transformers Are Not the End Game | World Models, Physical AI, and AI’s Next Frontier
episodes.summary: Recorded at NVIDIA GTC, Ksenia Se interviews Sanja Fidler, VP of AI Research at NVIDIA and head of its Spatial Intelligence Lab, about world models, spatial intelligence and physical AI. Fidler explains why transformers and world models are not competing, the evolution of driving simulation toward the interactive Alpa Dreams model, missing modalities like touch and radar, and when physical AI might have a ChatGPT moment.

episodes.title: The Calm Before the AGI Storm
episodes.summary: A news roundup NLW frames as the calm before the AGI storm: OpenAI closes a $122B round amid secondary-market weakness, executive shuffles, IPO tension and the TBPN acquisition; Anthropic faces a Claude Code source leak, usage-limit complaints and an OpenClaw subscription change. Also covers Gemma 4, Alibaba's proprietary Qwen 3.6 Plus, DeepSeek v4 on Huawei chips, Microsoft's models and Copilot, and the Iran war's effect on data centers. (Transcript contains a long repeated STT loop.)

episodes.title: 6 Questions Shaping AI
episodes.summary: A big-think episode on six questions shaping AI: job displacement, AI as a political issue, who decides AI's limits, the depth of infrastructure financing amid the Iran war, compounding differentiated enterprise adoption, and how much agency agents give people. NLW offers optimistic predictions on jobs and entrepreneurship.

episodes.title: The Masked Medici: How to Build a Faceless Youtube Channel and Companion 1990s Strategy Game in a Single Afternoon with Google AI
episodes.summary: In a Google-sponsored operators bonus episode, NLW builds a faceless Renaissance history YouTube channel, The Masked Medici, plus a companion web codex and a 1990s-style strategy game. He uses Gemini, NotebookLM cinematic video overviews, Stitch, and Google AI Studio, highlighting Google's integrated multimodal tools.

episodes.title: Training the AIs' Eyes: How Roboflow is Making the Real World Programmable, with CEO Joseph Nelson
episodes.summary: Nathan Labenz interviews Roboflow CEO Joseph Nelson about the state of computer vision, where frontier multimodal models still fail, and how teams distill large models into small edge-deployable ones. They discuss Roboflow's RF-DETR model and neural architecture search, open-source vision models from China, Meta and NVIDIA, agents and skills as a go-to-market, emerging trends like world models, VLAs and wearables, and regulating outcomes rather than tools.

episodes.title: How to Build a Personal Context Portfolio and MCP Server
episodes.summary: NLW proposes a personal context portfolio: a modular set of ten markdown files describing a person so any agent can use them, avoiding context lock-in. He shares GitHub templates, an Opus 4.6-powered interview app, and walks through building and deploying an MCP server for the portfolio with Claude's help.

episodes.title: Marc Andreessen introspects on The Death of the Browser, Pi + OpenClaw, and Why \"This Time Is Different\"
episodes.summary: Marc Andreessen argues the current AI wave is an "80-year overnight success" driven by four breakthroughs: LLMs, reasoning, agents and recursive self-improvement. He discusses the compute supply crunch and dot-com parallels, open source and China, Pi and OpenClaw as a Unix-style agent architecture, the future of programming and browsers, AI payments via crypto, proof of human, and why regulation and cartels will slow AI adoption.

episodes.title: AI for Atoms: How Periodic Labs is Revolutionizing Materials Engineering with Co-Founder Liam Fedus
episodes.summary: Elad Gil interviews Liam Fedus, co-creator of ChatGPT and co-founder of Periodic Labs, an AI foundation lab for atoms. Fedus discusses his path from physics through Google Brain to OpenAI, why AI science needs closed-loop physical experiments, using LLMs to orchestrate specialized atomic models, Periodic's commercialization as an intelligence layer for advanced manufacturing, and domain-specific recursive self-improvement.

episodes.title: Agent Skills Masterclass
episodes.summary: Nufar Gaspar walks through a five-level masterclass on agent skills, from what skills are to building organizational skill libraries. Topics include when to build skills, anatomy of an effective skill, example knowledge-worker skills, advanced patterns like dispatchers and chaining, testing, and org-level skill governance.

episodes.title: Moonlake: Causal World Models should be Multimodal, Interactive, and Efficient — with Chris Manning and Fan-yun Sun
episodes.summary: Moonlake co-founder Fan-yun Sun and Stanford NLP pioneer Chris Manning explain Moonlake's approach to world models: a multimodal reasoning model using symbolic abstractions and tools like game engines, plus the Reverie diffusion model for restyling. They contrast it with video-generation world models and Yann LeCun's JEPA, and discuss evaluation, spatial audio and hiring.

episodes.title: Uber’s Robotaxi Playbook, the End of Human Driving & $10B Bet on Robots | Dara Khosrowshahi (Uber CEO) | EP #244
episodes.summary: Audience Q&A with Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi at the 2026 Abundance360 Summit, hosted by Peter Diamandis with Salim Ismail. Topics include rider and regulator acceptance of autonomous vehicles, the future of human driving licenses, AV insurance, flying-car vertiports with Joby, Chinese AV partners, automation and jobs, EV adoption, and how Uber preserves its entrepreneurial culture and chooses new businesses.

episodes.title: Agentic Coding and the Economics of Open Source
episodes.summary: Chris Benson interviews Miklós Koren, economics professor at Central European University, about his paper 'Vibe Coding Kills Open Source'. Koren explains how AI agents divert scarce human attention away from open source maintainers, presents an experiment showing AI-recommended npm packages gain downloads but not GitHub stars, and discusses AI's effect on software engineering work and a more localized AI economy.

episodes.title: Introducing Maturity Maps — A New Way to Measure AI Adoption
episodes.summary: NLW introduces Superintelligent's AI maturity maps, a framework rating AI and agent maturity across six categories in ten business functions against an 'on-track' line. He shares Q2 findings drawn from 480+ studies, highlighting gaps in people investment, data, and outcome measurement.

episodes.title: Success without Dignity?  Nathan finds Hope Amidst Chaos, from The Intelligence Horizon Podcast
episodes.summary: A cross-post of Nathan Labenz's appearance on The Intelligence Horizon podcast with hosts Owen Zhang and Will Sanok Dufallo. Nathan discusses AGI timelines, RL scaling, LLM world models and interpretability, energy and chip bottlenecks, his p(doom) and modest optimism about alignment, defense-in-depth safety strategies, AI regulation, the Pentagon–Anthropic standoff, and US–China AI competition.

episodes.title: Coding The Natural World
episodes.summary: Astro Teller talks with Brad Zamft, CEO of X spin-out Heritable Agriculture, about using genomic and RNA data with machine learning to program crops for yield, pest and drought resistance. He then speaks with Relly Brandman, project lead of X's A-Life, about building an AI 'virtual cell' that moves biomanufacturing from trial and error to predictive design.

episodes.title: Scaling Uber with Thuan Pham (Uber’s first CTO)
episodes.summary: Gergely Orosz interviews Thuan Pham, Uber's first CTO and now CTO of Faire, about his path from Vietnamese refugee to HP Labs, Silicon Graphics, NetGravity and VMware, and his seven years scaling Uber. They cover Travis Kalanick's 30-hour interview, the dispatch rewrite, launching China in five months, the program/platform split, microservices and internal tools, Helix, career levels, and how Faire uses AI agents.
